verdict.asked_twice_evidence: No repeats. It caught the name and the problem from Maya's single turn ("I'm Maya... I'm constantly trying to keep up with all my kid's school emails") and never re-asked for either. Gmail was handled via the on-screen connect, never typed or spoken.
verdict.challenge_notes: For a pleasant baseline user it mostly delivered: fun name accepted with energy ("Love it! Scout it is."), help topic extracted from natural speech, immediate value shown with the Friday permission slip. Turn order was slightly off though \u2014 it asked "So what's got your attention most right now?" on the call before Maya had even answered the call-or-text question, so her "a call sounds great" landed as a non-sequitur. Wrap-up was also a declaration ("You're all set, Maya") rather than an offer, and the ending double-tapped ("Talk soon." / "Catch you later, Maya.").
verdict.made_things_up_evidence: After one honest label ("we're all set with demo data"), it dropped the framing entirely: "You've got the field trip due Friday, parent-teacher conference Sunday at four, and picture day next week." Those are presented as Maya's actual calendar \u2014 and a parent-teacher conference at 4pm on a Sunday is exactly the kind of fake detail that erodes trust. It also promised ongoing monitoring it hasn't established it can do: "I'll keep an eye on all of it."
verdict.best_moment: The pivot from problem to proof in one beat: "That's exactly what I can help with. We'll connect your Gmail and I'll pull all that stuff out for you" \u2192 "I can see you've got that field trip permission slip due Friday\u2014want me to flag that so it doesn't slip through?" That's value mid-flow, not a promise of value later.
verdict.worst_moment: Listing the Sunday parent-teacher conference and picture day as real commitments with no demo caveat, then saying "I'll keep an eye on all of it." A parent who trusts that and misses a real conference has been actively harmed by the demo.
